free_tier.stated: no service and no account; source and static builds

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: tcp

tooling: cargo, static builds in releases, AUR package
chaining: plain TCP or TLS, so it can ride a TCP forwarder that hands over a raw stream; it cannot ride an HTTP-only CDN because it never speaks an HTTP upgrade.
binding_note: the constraint is a server-side host, plus an unmaintained codebase, neither of which the vocabulary covers

identity_cost.detail: no account; a server-side daemon and a client-side daemon on hosts the operator controls

confidence_note: nothing would raise the maintenance rung; the last code change was 2020 and the last release tag is 'beta' from 2021

evidence.proved: the two modes and the -uh default of 127.0.0.1:51820 in client mode
release tag 'beta' published 2021-05-22; last push 2020-11-27; 96 stars

notes: Functionally the cleanest of the plain TCP wrappers and the only one whose TLS warning is honest about doing nothing by default. Five years without a commit makes it a reference implementation, not a recommendation. TLS mode needs a certificate at the server end.

extras.wg_detail: "Proxy wireguard UDP packets over TCP/TLS"; client mode listens on 127.0.0.1:51820 by default and the WireGuard peer points at it
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: server daemon pipes to the local WireGuard UDP port
extras.hosting_requirement: a publicly reachable host running the server daemon, plus the client daemon on the device
